definition: A rule that changes a graph by translating, reflecting or stretching it; the result is called the image.
A transformation that slides every point of a graph the same distance in the same direction, without turning or resizing it.
A transformation that flips a graph over a mirror line, such as the $x$-axis or the $y$-axis.
The transformation $y = pf(x)$, which multiplies every $y$-coordinate by the scale factor $p$ and keeps every $x$-coordinate.
The transformation $y = f(qx)$, which multiplies every $x$-coordinate by the scale factor $\frac{1}{q}$ and keeps every $y$-coordinate.
A point that a transformation leaves where it is, such as a point on the mirror line of a reflection.
